transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Eden), Liam O'Connor (Lead ML Eng, Eden), Sara Vogel (PM, Eden)

Auto-generated summary:
- Eden Platform is evaluating Redwood for a fast prototype (PLG/self-serve) with option to move to Dedicated or VPC for compliance later.
- Primary goals: time-to-first-token (TTFT) under 1 hour for devs, predictable latency for production, and data residency/controls for PHI-like telemetry.
- Next steps: share credits, security docs, run bench on sample prompts, schedule SE deep-dive.

Topics: quickstart credits, hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC), latency/cost tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS, rollout plan

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for taking time, um quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya Nair: yeah hi this is Priya from Eden, thanks Maya, Liam and Sara here too.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: hey, Liam.
[00:10] Sara Vogel: Sara, hi.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood, SE on the call.
[00:14] Maya Chen: awesome. quick agenda — 1) understand what you're building and success criteria, 2) explain Redwood quicklaunch credits and TTFT path, 3) call out security and hosting options, 4) agree next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Priya Nair: yep that's perfect. we're looking to prototype a contextual assistant inside Eden's admin console — low mem prompts initially but high QPS eventually, so latency and cost both matter.
[00:39] Liam O'Connor: to add — we want devs to be able to get to first call within a day, ideally under an hour for simple PoC. and we have a compliance bar — SOC2, SSO, and option for VPC in 2–3 months.
[00:52] Maya Chen: great, that aligns with a lot of customers. our PLG flow gives you self-serve API keys, free credits for quickstart, and a dev dashboard. for production, you can either reserve Dedicated capacity or lift into Private (VPC/on-prem) — sorry if I say Redwood Dedicate or Redwood Pri-vate, mis-say sometimes.
[01:10] Sara Vogel: quick question — how are you handling data retention and logs? we need to ensure logs can be turned off or routed to customer-managed storage.
[01:18] Diego Alvarez: good question. we have request-level data controls: option to disable logging, or forward audit logs to your Kinesis/S3 via our private link for Dedicated/Private. plus KMS integration for keys. sometimes the auto-transcript calls it K-V cache but that's separate from logs.
[01:35] Priya Nair: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)?
[01:38] Maya Chen: yes CMK supported in Private and in Dedicated via an enterprise integration. Hosted supports encryption at rest but for full CMK you would look at Private or a Dedicated arrangement with key sync.
[01:48] Liam O'Connor: for PoC, we'd prefer hosted self-serve to move fast; reserve capacity later if latencies don't hold. any gotchas?
[01:56] Diego Alvarez: main tradeoffs: hosted is fastest to TTFT, we give credits and a pre-configured model selection to minimize initial tuning. Dedicated gives you capacity guarantees and lower unit costs at scale, Private gives you network isolation and CMKs. note — model variants and quantization can change latency/cost.
[02:15] Maya Chen: do you have a sense of expected tokens per call and concurrency for the PoC?
[02:21] Liam O'Connor: currently avg 600 tokens per request, burst concurrency maybe 20–50 for dev tests, production later aiming 200–500 QPS.
[02:30] Diego Alvarez: ok 600 tokens average is helpful. with that payload, we can estimate rough token cost. we'll run a bench with your prompts.
[02:37] Sara Vogel: about the credits — what's in the quickstart credit pack?
[02:41] Maya Chen: we typically give a credits bundle that covers ~10k tokens of high-capacity model usage or equivalent configuration — basically enough to run a quick PoC. I'll send the exact bundle and a sample playbook.
[02:54] Priya Nair: cool. can we use those credits to test streaming responses? our UI uses streaming for token-by-token UI.
[03:01] Diego Alvarez: yes streaming supported on hosted API and Dedicated — function calls and streaming are in the API. small note: streaming latency is dependent on network and model chunking, we've seen consistent 150–300ms tail latencies for similar setups, but we'll validate with your prompt set.
[03:18] Liam O'Connor: you mentioned KV cache earlier — how does prefix caching work? could help reduce cost for repeated prompts.
[03:25] Diego Alvarez: prefix/KV cache caches decoder kvs for repeated contexts, so repeated system or instruction tokens can be avoided. it's automatic for many models, but semantics vary by architecture. it can drastically reduce per-token compute for chatty flows.
[03:40] Sara Vogel: and can that be used in Hosted?
[03:42] Diego Alvarez: yes, caching exists in hosted runtime; Dedicated gives you more control over cache retention sizes and explicit cache warm policies.
[03:50] [05:00] Speaker 2: (background) sorry—had to mute/unmute
[05:10] Priya Nair: switching to security — do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation? our security team will need evidence.
[05:17] Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC2 and we're working on ISO updates — I'll attach certs. for deeper concerns we can provide network diagrams and pen test reports under NDA.
[05:29] Liam O'Connor: what about SSO and RBAC for team access?
[05:33] Diego Alvarez: SSO via SAML/SCIM provisioning supported on the Console — role-based access and token scoping are there. Audit logs include token-level usage for billing/forensics.
[05:45] Sara Vogel: do you keep request transcripts for evals? privacy question.
[05:49] Maya Chen: by default we retain short logs for debugging but there is a opt-out; with Private you can route everything out, with Dedicated we have contract terms to limit retention.
[05:59] Priya Nair: timeline constraints — we need a PoC running in dev within two weeks. is that realistic?
[06:06] Diego Alvarez: absolutely for hosted. TTFT for a dev is often under an hour: sign up, create API key, drop in prompts. the two-week plan for production-ish tests is realistic if you allocate engineering time.
[06:18] Maya Chen: ok let's walk through a suggested rapid plan: Day 0–1: onboarding and credits; Day 1–3: integration tests (streaming, batching); Day 4–10: scale tests and SE bench; Day 11–14: decision on Dedicated/VPC.
[06:33] Liam O'Connor: can Diego run bench vs a small Dedicated slice so we can compare unit cost?
[06:37] Diego Alvarez: yes — I'll spin a small dev Dedicated profile or emulate with isolated hosted nodes; the comparison won't be exact but will show ballpark latency and cost delta.
[06:46] Sara Vogel: about pricing — do you have per-token for hosted and discounted reserved for Dedicated?
[06:50] Maya Chen: hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved with discounts depending on commit. I'll share a pricing matrix in the follow-up.
[06:58] Priya Nair: what's the minimum commit for Dedicated?
[07:01] Maya Chen: it depends on throughput needed, but typically teams start at a monthly equivalent of a few high-end GPUs; we'll propose a starter reserved plan to match your expected QPS.
[07:12] Liam O'Connor: curious about graceful degradation — if Dedicated hits capacity, do you fall back to Hosted?
[07:17] Diego Alvarez: yes routing policies can failover to hosted or to a smaller model variant; fallback is configurable per-route.
[07:26] [12:10] Maya Chen: (walk-through) I'll demo the API quick call — create key, curl request, receive streaming response — Liam feel free to ask if anything seems off.
[12:25] Liam O'Connor: is there an SDK for node/python?
[12:28] Diego Alvarez: yes we have official SDKs and examples; also a Postman collection in the docs.
[12:34] Sara Vogel: any limits on free accounts we should know?
[12:37] Maya Chen: rate limits for free tiers are lower; credits come with temporary higher limits for quickstart but we'll advise not to stress prod patterns on the credit account.
[12:46] Priya Nair: can you summarize network requirements for VPC? we have strict firewall rules.
[12:51] Diego Alvarez: VPC uses private peering and a control-plane handshake; we'll share the network diagram and firewall ports. you need to allow our control plane IPs for provisioning and a private link for inference traffic if you select that option.
[13:06] Liam O'Connor: does Private support on-prem? sometimes we have customer clusters.
[13:09] Maya Chen: yes on-prem packages exist but usually for larger enterprise deals; Private in VPC is more common in first wave.
[13:16] Priya Nair: what's the typical time to migrate from hosted to VPC?
[13:19] Diego Alvarez: typically 4–8 weeks depending on network setup and compliance review. we have a migration playbook.
[13:25] Sara Vogel: curious — any customers in finance/health using PHI-like data?
[13:30] Maya Chen: yes several in health are on Dedicated/Private with strict logging controls. we'll share anonymized case studies in the follow-up.
[13:39] Priya Nair: ok great. for the bench you'll need our prompt set — we'll anonymize and drop in the shared drive.
[13:45] Liam O'Connor: expectation is that you measure p50/p95 latencies and cost per 1k tokens, and include streaming tail latencies.
[13:54] Diego Alvarez: yep that's the plan. also will test with concurrency patterns.
[14:00] [18:05] Speaker 3: small interruption — laptop battery low
[18:12] Maya Chen: no problem. quick question for Priya — who else is the decision-maker for infra spend?
[18:18] Priya Nair: ultimately me and our Head of Ops (not on this call) — Sara will coordinate technical sign-off.
[18:24] Sara Vogel: correct.
[18:26] Maya Chen: ok great. last part — risks/objections: what are your top concerns?
[18:31] Priya Nair: performance parity and the unknowns around cost at scale.
[18:35] Liam O'Connor: also the test harness — we need reproducible benches.
[18:39] Diego Alvarez: understood. we'll produce a bench report with reproducible configs and raw metrics.
[18:44] Maya Chen: I'm going to send the quickstart playbook, security artifacts, and a pricing sheet. Diego will run the bench once you upload the prompts.
[18:52] Priya Nair: sounds good. can we get an approximate estimator now? even rough numbers would help us plan the meeting with finance.
[18:58] Maya Chen: for a 600-token average and dev QPS 20, hosted cost ballpark $0.10–0.30 per 1k tokens depending on model; Dedicated could reduce unit cost by 30–60% at scale — I'll put a clearer table in the follow-up. (note: numbers are illustrative)
[19:18] Liam O'Connor: helpful. thank you.
[19:21] Sara Vogel: one last thing — any pre-built evals for hallucination/regression monitoring?
[19:25] Diego Alvarez: yes Redwood Optimize and our eval hooks can run prompt-based regression tests and alert on quality drifts tied to models and rollouts. we can include a sample eval harness.
[19:36] Priya Nair: great.
[19:38] Maya Chen: ok to recap next steps: I'll send credits + docs by Monday 2026-05-11; Diego will run bench after prompt upload by 2026-05-13; we'll tentatively schedule the SE deep-dive on 2026-05-14 — does that work?
[19:51] Priya Nair: yes works for us.
[19:53] Liam O'Connor: good.
[19:55] Sara Vogel: thanks everyone.
[19:57] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with links.
[20:02] [46:30] Meeting end: informal wrap, small chatter and goodbyes
